unpinned_action.defect_claim: A workflow or composite action runs third-party action code through a mutable reference, so whoever can move that tag or branch decides what the step runs.
premises: The cited `uses:` names an external action whose ref is not a 40-character commit SHA (a tag, a branch, a short SHA or no ref).
The reference is not a local action (`./…`).

untrusted_workflow_interpolation.defect_claim: A workflow splices a value an outside party controls into `run:` shell source, where the runner substitutes it before bash parses it, so the value runs as code.
premises: The cited `${{ … }}` expression sits in a step's `run:` source, not in an `env:` or `with:` value.

The expression reads a workflow input (`inputs.*`, `github.event.inputs.*`) or an event field an outside author writes (a pull request's title, body or head branch, an issue or comment body, a commit message or author).

overbroad_write_token.defect_claim: A job's GITHUB_TOKEN can write more than the job needs, so a compromised step can write to scopes no step uses.
premises: The cited job's effective `permissions:` is `write-all`, or it grants `write` on a scope its job contract in aria-kernel/aria_kernel/workflow_contract_registry.py does not grant.
For a contract finding, the registry governs the cited job (its workflow file and job id).
For an ungoverned `contents: write` finding, no registry contract governs the cited job and no `reason:` comment beside the grant names why the write scope is needed.

pipe_to_shell.defect_claim: A step or script runs code it downloads without verifying it, so the server (or anyone on the path to it) chooses what runs with the job's credentials.
premises: The cited command pipes `curl` or `wget` output into a shell that reads its script from stdin, or passes it to a shell, `eval` or `source` as the script itself (`bash <(curl …)`, `sh -c "$(wget …)"`).
The command is executed (not inside a comment, a quoted string or a heredoc written to a file), and no checksum or signature check of the downloaded bytes happens before it runs.

governance_bypass_command.defect_claim: A workflow step or script force-pushes or skips git's hooks or signing, which the repository's rules forbid and ARIA's pre-PR-open perimeter refuses.
premises: The cited git command is refused by `governance_bypass_refusal` (aria-kernel/aria_kernel/implementation_safety.py): a forced push (`--force`, `--force-with-lease`, `-f`, a `+` refspec), or `--no-verify`, `--no-gpg-sign`, `commit -n`, or a `core.hooksPath` override.
The command is executed by the step or script (not inside a comment, a quoted string or a heredoc written to a file).

missing_strict_shell_mode.defect_claim: An executable Bash script runs on after a failed command or a failed pipeline stage, so it can act on a half-done step and report success.
premises: The cited file is an executable Bash script (a bash, zsh or ksh interpreter line and the executable bit) that runs more than one pipeline.
Neither its interpreter line nor a top-level `set` turns on each of errexit, nounset and pipefail.
It is not POSIX sh, a sourced fragment or a fixture.

command_substitution_in_message.defect_claim: A message printed by echo or printf names a command in backticks inside double quotes, so bash runs that command as a command substitution instead of printing its name.
premises: The cited `echo` or `printf` argument is double-quoted and holds an unescaped backtick pair; inside double quotes bash runs the text between the backticks as a command.

The command is executed by the step or script (not inside a comment, a single-quoted string or a heredoc written to a file), and the backticks name a command to print rather than a substitution the author meant (an intended substitution is written `$(…)`).
